message.content: Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that usually takes place over a period of several weeks. In practice, the tower’s maintenance schedule involves repainting every seven years or so, and the actual work is carried out in stages—first cleaning, then applying primer, followed by multiple coats of protective paint. A dedicated crew of painters working around the clock can finish the job in roughly 2–3 weeks, but the entire process—including preparation, inspection, and quality control—can extend to a month or more.
